text:
alex.support: FYI — Acme Tier2 reported intermittent SSE streams truncating when routed through their gRPC->HTTP1 Envoy gateway. Customer sees partial events then immediate socket close. They can repro consistently when their gateway converts h2->h1 for our endpoint.

alex.support: Repro curl they ran (we can run locally to confirm):
```
curl -v -N \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  --http2-prior-knowledge \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream?model=gpt-open-13b'
```

nina.support: Can you paste the exact first/last bytes we see? Also confirm whether Acme is using grpc-web or native gRPC->HTTP adapter.

alex.support: They say grpc-web client -> Envoy (http2) -> upstream our http1 edge. Attached small excerpt from client capture (truncated by customer):
```
data: {"id":1, "text":"Hello wor" 
// stream closed by gateway (RST_STREAM) before the rest comes in
```

envoy.bot: trace assigned: trace_id=9f3a2b7c-4e1a-11ee-8c99-0242ac120004 (ingress env-prod-eu1)

priya.sre: This matches a buffer/adapter behavior we've seen: Envoy's http2->http1 bridge may set Content-Length for upstream when downstream uses grpc-web framing and then close the connection early if it thought stream ended. Two quick asks: can we get gateway logs around trace_id above, and a tcpdump showing the 0-length chunk/FIN?

josh.eng-runtime: Also check whether our runtime is emitting "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" and flushing after each SSE event. If Envoy doesn't see chunked framing or if it buffers until upstream complete, it will coalesce and then close on mismatch. We had a similar case where trailing headers (trailers) were dropped and client interpreted EOF.

alex.support: Pasting gateway log snippet customer shared (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] trace=9f3a2b7c conn=12 downstream_proto=grpc-web upstream_proto=http/1.1 action=convert frame=DATA size=1024 upstream_response_code=200 bytes_sent=1024 stream_end=true
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] trace=9f3a2b7c conn=12 upstream_finish=RST_STREAM reason=stream_idle_timeout
```

maya.cust-success: Customer escalated because they say partial responses still billed; they want usage credits for the affected sessions. Can billing coordinate?

ben.billing: We'll need a list of request IDs or invoices. Alex, can you export sample request_ids and times (trace_id is helpful) so we can check tokenization counts vs charged tokens? We'll triage credits after verification.

josh.eng-runtime: Short-term workaround suggestions: 1) ask Acme to route SSE over plain HTTP/1.1 to our edge (disable h2 on client->envoy) or set their Envoy to preserve chunked transfer by enabling 'dechunk: false' equivalent. 2) Add header from client `X-Force-Chunked: 1` that we treat as hint to keep transfer-encoding chunked and flush frequently. 3) Upgrade envoy to >=1.24 where the h2->h1 stream handling bug is fixed.

priya.sre: Long term: we'll add an instrumentation metric sse.truncation.rate and alert when >0.1% for a canary, and we should implement more robust keepalive/frame heartbeat to ensure adapters don't infer EOF prematurely. Josh, can you open an eng-runtime issue with the trace and suggested change to ensure we always emit explicit chunk boundaries and a final 'event: done' marker before closing?

josh.eng-runtime: Will do. Proposed minimal config snippet for customers behind Envoy (suggest to send to Acme):
```
# Envoy HTTP connection manager snippet
http_filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.router
  typed_config: {}
stream_idle_timeout: 0s  # avoid idle RST during long-lived SSE
disable_chunked_encoding: false  # preserve chunked framing
```

alex.support: I will 1) ask Acme to try the HTTP/1.1 path as a canary, 2) collect request_ids for ben, 3) run an internal repro with grpc-web -> envoy -> our edge using their config and post tcpdumps.

maya.cust-success: Thanks — telling Acme we can fast-track a credit review once we have request_ids. Also offering to run a short live session with them to demonstrate workaround. :thumbsup:

ben.billing: thanks, I'll standby for the ID list.

nina.support: Adding note to the ticket: possible root causes = (a) envoy h2->h1 adapter setting content-length prematurely, (b) upstream not flushing chunk boundaries, (c) token expiry+reconnect causing 401 on reconnect — check for 401 patterns too.

alex.support: Good call on 401s — Acme also mentioned they see '401 on reconnect' sometimes when client reconnects after RST. Could be token rotation TTL. I'll add that to the log capture ask.

priya.sre: Ok plan: reproduce internally (priority), validate fix in canary (envoy config or runtime change), roll fix to production window, and coordinate credits with billing. Assigning owners: josh.eng-runtime (fix + issue), priya.sre (canary + metrics), alex.support (customer comm + repro artifacts), ben.billing (credit eval).

alex.support: Copying plan to Acme and will post the internal repro artifacts here when ready.

maya.cust-success: keeping customer updated. closing loop after repro.
